shortDescription: Measure Windows processes and Android apps locally with live performance charts and clear, exportable reports.
description:
LumaTrace Performance Lab is a local-first desktop performance testing tool for Windows and Android workflows.

Choose a Windows process or an Android app on an authorized ADB device, start a test, and follow the measurements that are available for that target. Finish the test to review a clear summary and export HTML, JSON, and CSV reports.

LumaTrace keeps test data on your computer by default. It does not require a cloud account and does not upload your measurements to a LumaTrace cloud service. Optional session-log export is disabled by default and writes bounded, sanitized logs only when you select it for a test.

Metric availability depends on the platform, device, drivers, local tools, and permissions. LumaTrace labels every measurement with its source and availability. Missing measurements remain N/A and are never replaced with invented values.
features: Select and measure a Windows process on the local computer
Test an Android app through an ADB connection authorized by the user
View live charts for measurements that are available
Review FPS, CPU, GPU, memory, power, temperature, and network data when supported
Export a separate HTML, JSON, and CSV report folder for each test
Keep optional sanitized session logs in the user-selected report directory
Inspect measurement source, precision, confidence, and availability
Delete completed local test results individually or in bulk
releaseNotesReason: Leave blank for the first Store submission.
certificationNotes: Base Windows testing runs as the current user and does not require administrator privileges.
For a Windows smoke test, open Run Test, choose Windows, select a visible process, start the test, wait for available data, and stop the test.
Android testing is optional and requires an Android device with developer options and USB debugging enabled, user authorization for this computer, and a working local ADB installation.

FPS and hardware telemetry depend on the selected target, supported local tools, drivers, and permissions. Unavailable measurements are shown as N/A and do not prevent CPU or memory testing when those sources remain available.
The desktop application communicates with its companion service only through a loopback address on the same computer.

Optional session-log export is off by default. When selected, Android produces bounded and sanitized target-filtered ADB logcat, while Windows produces sanitized LumaTrace session events in the selected report directory.
Reports are written to the user-selected report directory. No LumaTrace cloud account or cloud upload is required.
